```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                       fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines) for equation manipulation /
# show-your-work; pair with fig.height set to however much room is needed
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. Emits nothing in non-LaTeX output. lines =
# lines of prompt text, rows = rows of blank space below it (0.3 in each),
# extra = any other height (in inches), e.g. a figure or table
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}

beetles <- read.csv("../../data/BeetleFumigation.csv")
x <- beetles$log10_dose
n_exposed <- beetles$beetles
killed <- beetles$killed

nll_ld50 <- function(par) {
  -sum(dbinom(killed, size = n_exposed, prob = plogis(par[2] * (x - par[1])), log = TRUE))
}
check_val <- nll_ld50(c(1.75, 30))
check_val_nc <- check_val - sum(lchoose(n_exposed, killed))
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

```{r key-values, include=FALSE}
f2 <- function(v, d = 2) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d)
log_choose <- sum(lchoose(n_exposed, killed))
fit2 <- optim(c(1.77, 34), nll_ld50, hessian = TRUE)
se_L <- sqrt(diag(solve(fit2$hessian)))[1]
wald_L <- fit2$par[1] + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_L
L_grid <- seq(1.755, 1.790, by = 0.0001)
prof <- sapply(L_grid, function(L) optimize(function(b) nll_ld50(c(L, b)), c(5, 80))$objective)
dprof <- prof - fit2$value
prof_L <- range(L_grid[dprof <= qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2])
nll_ld99 <- function(par) {
  -sum(dbinom(killed, n_exposed, plogis(par[2] * (x - par[1]) + qlogis(0.99)), log = TRUE))
}
fit99 <- optim(c(1.9, 34), nll_ld99)
L99_grid <- seq(1.86, 1.98, by = 0.0002)
prof99 <- sapply(L99_grid, function(L) optimize(function(b) nll_ld99(c(L, b)), c(5, 80))$objective)
prof_L99 <- range(L99_grid[prof99 - fit99$value <= qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2])
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta.}


## The scenario

A pest manager has seen the fumigation results from Act 1 and wants to
know the dose that kills half the beetles (the **LD50**) in mg/L, with
a 95% interval. The model from Act 1 has no LD50 parameter; the LD50 is
a function of $a$ and $b$. In this Act you rewrite the model so that
$L$, the LD50 on the log10 dose scale, appears as a parameter. You then
build two intervals for $L$ (one from the Hessian, one from the
likelihood profile) and convert them to mg/L at the end
($\text{LD50} = 10^L$).

**How uncertain is the LD50, and do the two methods agree?**

Try Part 1 on paper first, before you open a laptop or start typing
code.


## Part 1: Plan it on paper (individual, ~20 min)

**1a.** Act 1 used the model
$$\log\frac{p}{1-p} = a + b\,x,$$
where $p$ is the probability that a beetle dies at log10 dose $x$. Let
$L$ be the log10 dose at which $p = 0.5$. Find $L$ in terms of $a$ and
$b$, and show that this model can be rewritten as
$\log\frac{p}{1-p} = b\,(x - L)$. Then use Act 1's MLEs
($\hat a = -60.72$, $\hat b = 34.27$) to estimate $L$, and convert your
estimate to mg/L.

\ans{$p = 0.5$ means log-odds $= 0$: $a + bL = 0$, so $L = -a/b$. Then $a + bx = b(x + a/b) = b(x - L)$.}

$\hat L \approx$ \ans{$60.72/34.27 \approx `r f2(60.72 / 34.27, 3)`$} (log10 dose) \qquad LD50 $= 10^{\hat L} \approx$ \ans{`r f2(10^(60.72 / 34.27), 1)`} mg/L


**1b.** Write the negative log-likelihood, $\text{NLL}(L, b)$, for the
eight doses. You can drop terms that don't depend on $L$ or $b$.

\ansbegin

$$\text{NLL}(L, b) = -\sum_{i=1}^{8}\left[k_i \log p_i + (n_i - k_i)\log(1 - p_i)\right], \qquad p_i = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-b(x_i - L)}}$$

($k_i$ killed of $n_i$ exposed at dose $i$; the $\log\binom{n_i}{k_i}$ terms are dropped.)

\ansend


**1c.** In plain English (not R code), describe step by step how you
would compute the likelihood profile for $L$ and read a 95% interval
off it. (Recall how the profile differed from the slice in Act 1.)

\ans{Choose a grid of $L$ values around $\hat L$. For each, hold $L$ fixed and find the $b$ that minimizes the NLL; record that minimum. Subtract the overall minimum NLL (at the MLE). The 95\% interval runs from the smallest to the largest $L$ whose value is 1.92 or less.}


## Checkpoint: finalize your plan (~5 min)

Look back over 1a-1c and fix anything that no longer looks right
before you start coding.

**2a.** *(Recommended: no AI.)* Write an NLL function whose first
argument is `par = c(L, b)`. Check it: at $L = 1.75$, $b = 30$ it should
return about `r round(check_val, 2)` if you used `dbinom()`, or about
`r round(check_val_nc, 2)` if you coded the formula yourself and dropped
the constant. Then fit it with `optim(..., hessian = TRUE)`, starting
from your values in 1a. Use `solve()` on the Hessian to get the
variance-covariance matrix; the square roots of its diagonal are the
standard errors. Report the 95% quadratic interval,
$\hat L \pm 1.96\,\text{SE}$.

$\hat L =$ \ans{`r f2(fit2$par[1], 4)`} \quad $\hat b =$ \ans{`r f2(fit2$par[2])`} \quad NLL at the MLE: \ans{`r f2(fit2$value)` (or `r f2(fit2$value - log_choose)` without the constant)}

$\text{SE}(\hat L) =$ \ans{`r f2(se_L, 4)`} \quad interval for $L$: \ans{`r f2(wald_L[1], 4)`} to \ans{`r f2(wald_L[2], 4)`}

AI use (circle one): no AI / AI helped (e.g., debugging) / AI wrote the code


**2b.** *(Recommended: no AI.)* Implement your profile from 1c and
report the 95% profile interval for $L$. How does it compare with 2a?

Profile interval for $L$: \ans{`r f2(prof_L[1], 4)`} to \ans{`r f2(prof_L[2], 4)`}

\ans{Nearly identical to the quadratic interval from 2a.}

```{r ans-profile, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3}
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 0.5, 0.5))
plot(L_grid, dprof, type = "l", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 4), col = ans_col,
     xlab = "L (log10 dose)", ylab = "Profile NLL minus its minimum")
abline(h = qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2)
abline(v = prof_L, lty = 2, col = ans_col)
abline(v = wald_L, lty = 3)
legend("top", c("profile interval", "Hessian interval"), lty = c(2, 3),
       col = c(ans_col, "black"), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

AI use (circle one): no AI / AI helped (e.g., debugging) / AI wrote the code


**2c.** *(AI optional/encouraged.)* Plot your profile. Put $L$ on the
x-axis. On the y-axis, put the profile NLL at each value of $L$ minus
the smallest profile NLL, so the lowest point of the curve is at zero.
Add a horizontal line at 1.92 and mark both intervals (from 2a and 2b).
Then convert $\hat L$ and the profile interval to mg/L.

LD50 $= 10^{\hat L}$: \ans{`r f2(10^fit2$par[1], 1)`} mg/L, from \ans{`r f2(10^prof_L[1], 1)`} to \ans{`r f2(10^prof_L[2], 1)`} mg/L

99% of beetles, $L_{99}$, satisfies
$\log\frac{p}{1-p} = b\,(x - L_{99}) + \log\frac{0.99}{0.01}$. Profile

\ans{$\hat L_{99} \approx `r f2(fit99$par[1], 3)`$ (`r f2(10^fit99$par[1], 1)` mg/L); profile interval `r f2(10^prof_L99[1], 1)` to `r f2(10^prof_L99[2], 1)` mg/L, about `r round(diff(prof_L99) / diff(prof_L))` times as wide (log scale) as the LD50's.}

## Reflection (~10 min)

Suppose the pest manager wants a dose that kills 99% of beetles instead
of 50%. Without computing anything, would you expect its interval to be
wider or narrower than the LD50's? (Look at where the data sit in Act
1's figure.) The Hessian and profile intervals nearly agreed here. When
would you expect them to disagree? Think back to the chytrid curve from
Monday's WOD.

Also record any changes you made, new insights, and any "muddiest
points" or topics you want to review.

\ans{Wider: the LD99 lies above the highest dose tested, where batches can only show "nearly all died," and it depends heavily on the slope. The Hessian and profile intervals disagree when the NLL isn't close to a parabola: small samples, estimates near a boundary (like prevalence near 0 in the chytrid WOD), or quantities outside the range of the data.}
